## On-Call Handoff — Gateway 503s

**Root cause:** dep-4471 (gateway, a.novak, 2026-03-14T02:12:00Z–02:14:00Z) — "config: connection-per-request for pool isolation." This flipped `gateway.pool.perRequest` from `false` to `true` (config generation 119, applied 02:13:41.234Z). Shortly after, the connection pool (fixed size 20) began saturating — every request now claims its own connection instead of sharing — and has never recovered, with the wait queue climbing steadily (13 → 74+ by 03:59Z, last log entry).

**Impact window:** Started 2026-03-14T02:14:18.972Z (first 503, req-07401, `/v1/cart -> billing-svc`), ongoing as of the last log line at 03:59:27Z. No recovery observed. Affects all gateway-routed traffic (`/v1/cart`, `/v1/session`, `/v1/catalog/search`, `/v1/orders`, `/v1/checkout`) across billing-svc, orders-svc, catalog-svc, accounts-svc. `/health` checks still return 200, so basic health probes won't catch this.

**Error signature:**
```
ERROR pool req-XXXXX ERR_POOL_EXHAUSTED acquiring connection from pool (size 20, in_use 20, waiting N)
```

**Scope check:** Worker service (logs/worker.log) unaffected — separate DB pool, all jobs completed normally through and after the incident window. This is gateway-only.

**Action:** Roll back dep-4471 (revert `gateway.pool.perRequest` to `false`), or push a new config generation restoring the prior pool-sharing behavior. Two later deploys shipped after the incident began — dep-4472 (billing-svc, 02:41Z) and dep-4473 (catalog-svc, 03:20Z) — neither touches gateway/pool config, no rollback needed on those.
